messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning: The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate something about hypothesis testing. They mention sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, null hypothesis population mean 98.6. They ask: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They likely want to compute the standard error or the t-statistic? They mention "零假設檢定的標準差" which might be the standard error of the mean under null? Or they want to compute the p-value? The user didn't specify significance level. They might want to compute the standard error: SE = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So SE ≈ 0.2213. Then t-statistic: (sample_mean - population_mean) / SE = (98.2 - 98.6) / 0.2213 = (-0.4) / 0.2213 ≈ -1.807. So t ≈ -1.807. Degrees of freedom df = n-1 = 39. Then p-value two-tailed: 2 * P(T <= -1.807) with df=39. Let's approximate using t distribution. For df=39, t=1.807. The p-value maybe around 0.08? Let's approximate: For df=40, t=1.68 gives p=0.10; t=2.02 gives p=0.05. So t=1.807 gives p ~ 0.08. So two-tailed p ~ 0.08. So we fail to reject null at alpha=0.05 but reject at alpha=0.10. But the user didn't ask for p-value. They asked: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They might want to compute the standard error of the mean under null? Or the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean? That is indeed the standard error. So answer: Standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.221. Then t-statistic = (98.2-98.6)/0.221 ≈ -1.81. Then p-value ~ 0.08. So we can provide that. Also we can mention that the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean is 0.221. So we can answer accordingly.
